sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报栏目 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场，采访一些商业、政治和文化领域举足轻重的领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼（Zilron Mondani）以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费权限来阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不会想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: The White House response to the impeachment inquiry has been to dismiss the allegations, deflect the facts, and discredit the Democrats.
sentences.zh: 白宫对弹劾调查的回应一直是驳斥指控、转移事实并抹黑民主党人。

sentences.en: It's the same approach used by Republicans in 2018 to push through the Supreme Court nomination of Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 这与共和党人在2018年强行通过布雷特·卡瓦诺最高法院提名的手法如出一辙。

sentences.en: My colleagues Kate Kelly and Robin
sentences.zh: 我的同事凯特·凯利和罗宾

sentences.en: Pogger, the authors of The Education of Brett Kavanaugh, talked to the Republican strategist who wrote the political playbook used then and now.
sentences.zh: 波格（Pogger），《布雷特·卡瓦诺的教育》一书的作者，采访了当时和现在都在撰写政治剧本的共和党战略家。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, October 10th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月10日，星期四。

sentences.en: Robin, Kate, how did you first come to hear the name Mike Davis?
sentences.zh: 罗宾，凯特，你们是怎么第一次听到迈克·戴维斯这个名字的？

sentences.en: So we were looking back on the events of 2018 that were just so seismic for the country
sentences.zh: 所以我们回顾了2018年的那些对国家具有极其震撼意义的事件，

sentences.en: and trying to really slow down time and figure out very much from a 360-degree perspective who were the key players in that drama.
sentences.zh: 并试图真正放慢时间，从全方位、立体的角度去弄清楚这场戏剧中的关键人物都是谁。

sentences.en: Obviously, you had then Judge Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 显然，当时有法官卡瓦诺。

sentences.en: You had the women who had accused him of sexual misconduct and lawyers on both sides.
sentences.zh: 还有指控他性行为不端的女性以及双方的律师。

sentences.en: But the political machinery, who were the important members of the Senate Judiciary Committee?
sentences.zh: 但政治机器方面，参议院司法委员会的重要成员都有谁？

sentences.en: And everyone said we should talk to this one operative, that he was at the center of everything.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说我们应该去跟这位特工谈谈，他处于所有事情的中心。

sentences.en: And that operative's name was Mike Davis.
sentences.zh: 而这位特工的名字叫迈克·戴维斯。

sentences.en: Hey, is that Robin or is that Kate?
sentences.zh: 嘿，那是罗宾还是凯特？

sentences.en: That was Kate just now, but Robin's right here.
sentences.zh: 刚刚那是凯特，不过罗宾就在这儿。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: And everybody told us that he was sort of an unabashed advocate for Judge Kavanaugh and really sort of the torch carrier politically through this process.
sentences.zh: 每个人都告诉我们，他可以说是法官卡瓦诺毫不掩饰的支持者，也是这个过程中实际上在政治上高举火炬的人。

sentences.en: And what he did in terms of not just managing the technicalities of the Senate investigation in the Senate process, but also
sentences.zh: 他在处理参议院调查和参议院程序的具体技术细节方面不仅如此，而且

sentences.en: waging this sort of cultural war for conservatives that was crystallized during the Kavanaugh confirmation process and is now being deployed as a defense against impeachment.
sentences.zh: 为保守派发起了一场文化战争，这场战争在卡瓦诺确认听证会期间具象化，现在正被用作抵御弹劾的防御手段。

sentences.en: So you knew that you wanted to talk to him?
sentences.zh: 所以你们就知道自己想采访他了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so in talking to him, you know, he actually turns out to be somewhat of an unlikely character.
sentences.zh: 所以在和他交谈时，你知道，他其实是个有点出人意料的人物。

sentences.en: And would like to start by just asking you, tell us about your career background.
sentences.zh: 并想先问你一个问题，跟我们讲讲你的职业背景吧。

sentences.en: How did you decide to become a lawyer?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么决定成为一名律师的？

sentences.en: Ever since I was a little kid, I think my teachers, the priests, the nuns at my
sentences.zh: 从小时候起，我想我的老师们，神父，还有我

sentences.en: Catholic school knew that I was going to be a lawyer just because I was so mouthy as a kid.
sentences.zh: 天主教学校的修女们就知道我会成为一名律师，只因为我小时候太能说会道了。

sentences.en: He's kind of a spark plug of a guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个像火花塞一样精力充沛的家伙。

sentences.en: He's sort of built compactly.
sentences.zh: 他身材略显敦实。

sentences.en: He's very much of a kind of a tough talker.
sentences.zh: 他非常有那种说话强硬的风格。

sentences.en: He takes no prisoners.
sentences.zh: 他毫不留情。

sentences.en: But he was born and raised in Iowa.
sentences.zh: 但他是在艾奥瓦州出生并长大的。

sentences.en: So I was raised by two very liberal Democrats who worked in public schools.
sentences.zh: 所以我是在两个在公立学校工作的非常自由派的民主党人抚养下长大的。

sentences.en: And so I was raised very working class.
sentences.zh: 所以我的成长环境非常工薪阶层。

sentences.en: I was raised Catholic.
sentences.zh: 我是天主教徒。

sentences.en: So I had, you know, the bleeding heart Catholic stuff for my mom.
sentences.zh: 所以我身上有，你知道的，我母亲传给我的那种悲天悯人的天主教情怀。

sentences.en: And he had his own kind of awakening in terms of conservative issues.
sentences.zh: 而他在保守派议题上也有他自己的一种觉醒。

sentences.en: You know, I've always been kind of a right wing lunatic, even from a young age.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我从小到大一直有点像个右翼狂热分子。

sentences.en: And even in sixth grade, he won the Alex P.
sentences.zh: 甚至在六年级时，他还赢得了亚历克斯·P.

sentences.en: Keaton Award.
sentences.zh: 基顿奖。

sentences.en: Alex P.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·P.

sentences.en: Keaton, of course, being a reference to the beloved 1980s sitcom Family Ties, where you have two bleeding heart liberal parents in Ohio with a large family.
sentences.zh: 基顿，当然是指20世纪80年代备受喜爱的情景喜剧《天才家庭》（Family Ties），剧中俄亥俄州有一对心软的自由派父母，他们有许多孩子。

sentences.en: And they have this super conservative son, Alex P.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个超级保守的儿子，亚历克斯·P.

sentences.en: Keaton, who like loves Reaganomics and is like a total black sheep within that context.
sentences.zh: 基顿，他喜欢里根经济学，在这种背景下简直是个彻头彻尾的异类。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Bounds into the kitchen every morning in his tie and his jacket.
sentences.zh: 每天早上都系着领带、穿着夹克冲进厨房。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like raving about Reagan.
sentences.zh: 就像对里根赞不绝口一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I saw the effects of these policies that that liberals, that Democrats thought were helping people who needed help.
sentences.zh: 我看到了这些政策的影响，自由派、民主党人认为这些政策在帮助需要帮助的人。

sentences.en: And they actually trap people in intergenerational poverty.
sentences.zh: 而它们实际上把人们困在了跨代贫困之中。

sentences.en: So for me, that was the reason I became Republican is as I saw.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，这就是我成为共和党人的原因，因为我看到了。

sentences.en: And so then by college, he is working as an intern for Newt Gingrich, who kind of defined the outer edges of Republican philosophy at the time with the Contract for
sentences.zh: 因此到了大学时，他正在为纽特·金里奇担任实习生，金里奇当时通过《与美国契约》

sentences.en: America.
sentences.zh: 界定了共和党哲学的边缘。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Which is a very much less government is better approach.
sentences.zh: 这是一种政府越少越好的方法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Hands off.
sentences.zh: 放手不管。

sentences.en: And he kind of becomes really sort of evangelized in a way.
sentences.zh: 他某种程度上真正地被“洗礼”了，以某种方式。

sentences.en: And he wants to be a soldier.
sentences.zh: 他想成为一名士兵。

sentences.en: My first job in Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 我在华盛顿特区的第一份工作

sentences.en: was back in 1998 as an undergraduate intern working in the office of
sentences.zh: 是在1998年，当时作为一名本科实习生在众议院

sentences.en: House Speaker Newt Gingrich.
sentences.zh: 议长纽特·金里奇的办公室工作。

sentences.en: And while he works for Newt Gingrich, the Clinton impeachment is going on.
sentences.zh: 在为纽特·金里奇工作期间，克林顿弹劾案正在进行。

sentences.en: So Mike Davis has a front row seat on that strategy and it makes a strong impression on him.
sentences.zh: 因此迈克·戴维斯对这一战略有了近距离的观察，这给他留下了深刻的印象。

sentences.en: I remember watching this up close and personally.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己近距离且亲历了这一切。

sentences.en: My last day of my internship was the same day that the House of Representatives voted to impeach
sentences.zh: 我实习的最后一天，恰好是众议院投票弹劾

sentences.en: President Clinton.
sentences.zh: 克林顿总统的同一天。

sentences.en: And he's watching all of this going on.
sentences.zh: 他目睹了这一切的发生。

sentences.en: He's very intrigued by it.
sentences.zh: 他对此非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: And he's taking notes as to how these processes are unfolding and how the parties are reshaping themselves in the early to mid-90s.
sentences.zh: 他在做笔记，记录这些程序是如何展开的，以及在90年代初到中期各党派是如何重塑自己的。

sentences.en: So the impeachment of Bill Clinton would have been Mike Davis's first culture war, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 所以对迈克·戴维斯来说，比尔·克林顿的弹劾可以说是他的第一场文化战争。

sentences.en: And it sounds like he was very closely paying attention to it.
sentences.zh: 听起来他一直在非常密切地关注这件事。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, he's becoming a keen observer of politics.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他正在成为一个敏锐的政治观察家。

sentences.en: He has worked a stint for Iowa Senator Chuck Grassley opening mail.
sentences.zh: 他曾为艾奥瓦州参议员查克·格拉斯利工作过一段时间，负责拆信。

sentences.en: That was in May of 2000.
sentences.zh: 那是在2000年5月。

sentences.en: I was 20, 22 years old, right out of school.
sentences.zh: 我当时20、22岁，刚毕业。

sentences.en: He works in the Justice Department for a spell.
sentences.zh: 他在司法部工作了一阵子。

sentences.en: He goes to law school, becomes a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他去读了法学院，成了一名律师。

sentences.en: And he decides he wants to engage with all of these issues and he's going to do it from various angles.
sentences.zh: 他决定参与所有这些议题，并且他打算从各个角度切入。

sentences.en: And at some point he meets Neil Gorsuch.
sentences.zh: 在某个时候，他遇到了尼尔·戈萨奇。

sentences.en: He was in private practice and I helped him find his way into the Justice Department and then his way onto the 10th Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver, Colorado.
sentences.zh: 他当时在私人事务所工作，我帮他找到了进入司法部的途径，然后又帮他进入了位于科罗拉多州丹佛市的第十巡回上诉法院。

sentences.en: Gorsuch is named to the 10th Circuit Court in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇被任命为科罗拉多州第十巡回法院法官。

sentences.en: Then when Neil Gorsuch got confirmed as Judge Gorsuch, he asked me to go out to Colorado to clerk for him.
sentences.zh: 后来尼尔·戈萨奇被确认为戈萨奇法官时，他邀请我去科罗拉多州给他当法官助理。

sentences.en: So I went out to Colorado for a year.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了科罗拉多州待了一年。

sentences.en: Davis clerks for him.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯担任他的助理。

sentences.en: And I liked it so much that I stayed out there.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢那里了，所以就留在了那儿。

sentences.en: I was in the private practice of law for 10 years.
sentences.zh: 我从事私人法律业务有10年之久。

sentences.en: Davis very early on sees a lot of potential in Gorsuch, sees him as someone, you know, he would like to align himself with and maybe help promote from behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯很早就看到了戈萨奇身上的巨大潜力，认为他是一个自己愿意与之结盟、并或许可以从幕后协助推选的人。

sentences.en: And he remains close to Judge Gorsuch for a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 并且他与戈萨奇法官长期保持着密切联系。

sentences.en: And what do you think that Davis sees in Gorsuch?
sentences.zh: 你认为戴维斯在戈萨奇身上看到了什么？

sentences.en: Why is he latching on to him?
sentences.zh: 他为什么紧抓着他不放？

sentences.en: So what Mike Davis sees in Neil Gorsuch is kind of the embodiment of these values that
sentences.zh: 所以迈克·戴维斯在尼尔·戈萨奇身上看到的是一种价值观的化身，

sentences.en: Mike Davis has come to care about and be committed to.
sentences.zh: 这些价值观正是迈克·戴维斯开始关心并致力于的。

sentences.en: And Neil Gorsuch is kind of the perfect candidate right out of central casting.
sentences.zh: 而尼尔·戈萨奇可以说是从中央选角库里走出来的完美候选人。

sentences.en: He not only has hard and strong conservative values, but he's kind of unapologetic about them in a way that Mike Davis feels enables him to go the distance.
sentences.zh: 他不仅有着坚定而强烈的保守派价值观，而且他对此毫不掩饰，迈克·戴维斯觉得这使他能够走得更远。

sentences.en: And Mike Davis realizes that changing the judiciary is the strongest avenue towards making lasting change in this country.
sentences.zh: 迈克·戴维斯意识到，改变司法机关是推动这个国家实现持久变革的最有力途径。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 为什么这么说？

sentences.en: Because those are judges who are many of these appointments are for life.
sentences.zh: 因为这些法官中，许多任命都是终身制的。

sentences.en: And this is the time when you're making laws that are very difficult to change once you've made them as opposed to political administrations that can come and go.
sentences.zh: 而且这是一个制定法律的时期，一旦制定，与来来往往的政治行政当局相比，这些法律将非常难以改变。

sentences.en: So this becomes the strategy, which is to confirm as many judges as possible as quickly as you can within kind of an ideological framework that fits with his values.
sentences.zh: 所以这就成了策略，那就是在符合他价值观的意识形态框架内，尽可能快地确认尽可能多的法官。

sentences.en: So it's kind of Alex P.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像是把亚历克斯·P·

sentences.en: Keaton woven into the law through judges like Neil Gorsuch.
sentences.zh: 基顿通过尼尔·戈萨奇这样的法官编织进法律里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So when the Trump administration begins, there's this historic opportunity to fill the seat vacated
sentences.zh: 因此，当特朗普政府开始时，出现了一个历史性的机会，来填补因保守派大法官斯卡利亚去世而空出的席位

sentences.en: by the conservative Justice Scalia, who has died the year prior and whose seat has not been filled.
sentences.zh: 斯卡利亚于前一年去世，其席位一直空缺。

sentences.en: Gorsuch is someone that Davis regards as an ideal choice to add to the court.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇被戴维斯视为加入最高法院的理想人选。

sentences.en: So Davis is instrumental in helping Gorsuch sort of get on the map in terms of a potential nominee.
sentences.zh: 因此，戴维斯在帮助戈萨奇作为潜在提名人崭露头角方面发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: Gorsuch is nominated.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇获得提名。

sentences.en: Davis then takes on the role of assisting Gorsuch from the outside through the nomination process as a
sentences.zh: 作为前任书记员、朋友、多年来在法律界有着共同政府经验的同事，戴维斯随后承担起在提名过程中从外部协助戈萨奇的角色。

sentences.en: former clerk, a friend, a sort of colleague in legal circles for a number of years with shared government experience.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇获得确认。

sentences.en: Gorsuch is confirmed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，39岁的戴维斯被邀请在戈萨奇加入最高法院的残余任期内担任其书记员。

sentences.en: And in fact, Davis is asked at age 39 to clerk for Gorsuch on the Supreme Court for the sort of stub term that Gorsuch enters into.
sentences.zh: 我是一个挺老的高级法律书记员，39岁，推着助行器在最高法院走来走去。

sentences.en: I was a pretty old law clerk, 39 years old, walking around with my walker around the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 所以他有这段经历。

sentences.en: So he has that experience.
sentences.zh: 然后有一个空缺，可以担任为参议院司法委员会的格拉斯利工作的首席提名顾问。

sentences.en: And then there's this opening to be the chief nominations counsel working for Grassley on the Senate Judiciary Committee.
sentences.zh: 此时，戴维斯作为顽强的拥护者和熟练的政治运作者的声誉已经巩固。

sentences.en: And Davis's reputation by now is cemented as sort of a dogged advocate and a skilled political operator.
sentences.zh: 现在他准备好从内部参与潜在的最高法院

sentences.en: And now he's poised to work on potential Supreme
sentences.zh: 提名工作，这将从内部协助保守派多数派。

sentences.en: Court nominations that will aid the conservative majority from the inside.
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克，请把我们带回到2018年6月。

sentences.en: So take us back, Mike, to June 2018.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪大法官出人意料地宣布辞职。

sentences.en: Justice Kennedy surprisingly announces his resignation.
sentences.zh: 你当时的反应是什么？

sentences.en: What is your reaction at the time?
sentences.zh: 你接下来的举动是什么？

sentences.en: And then what is your next move?
sentences.zh: 我非常兴奋。

sentences.en: I was very excited.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是巩固法院保守派多数派的历史性机遇。

sentences.en: I thought it was a historic opportunity to solidify a conservative majority on the court.
sentences.zh: 我那天在想，这就是为什么

sentences.en: I was thinking that day, this is the reason that
sentences.zh: 共和党人、独立人士，甚至一些头脑清醒的民主党人投票支持特朗普总统的原因，因为这个空缺是如此重要。

sentences.en: Republicans, that independents, even some right thinking Democrats voted for President Trump because of how important this vacancy would be.
sentences.zh: 这是终极胜利，因为一旦你在法院拥有了5比4的多数派，并且你取代了作为摇摆票的安东尼·肯尼迪，你现在就

sentences.en: And it's the ultimate victory because once you have a 5-4 majority on the court and you're replacing Anthony Kennedy, who was a swing vote, you will now have

sentences.en: cemented this conservative shift, which is the ultimate goal for the Republicans.

sentences.zh: 因此，当布雷特·卡瓦诺被提名时，查克·格拉斯利招募了迈克·戴维斯作为他强硬的手段

sentences.en: So when Brett Kavanaugh is nominated, Chuck Grassley enlists Mike Davis as his kind of brass knuckles to
sentences.zh: 来确保这笔交易达成，让这家伙冲过终点线，并巩固最高法院的保守派多数派。

sentences.en: make sure to close this deal, bring this guy over the finish line and cement the conservative majority on the high court.
sentences.zh: 我绝不可能让这位好人卡瓦诺法官受到这些虚假

sentences.en: There was no way I was going to let this good man, Justice Kavanaugh, get smeared with these bogus
sentences.zh: 指控和谎言的玷污，因为，你知道，有些人担心他在罗伊诉韦德案上会做出某种裁决。

sentences.en: allegations and lies because, you know, some people are fearful that he's going to rule a certain way on Roe versus Wade.

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 因为迈克·戴维斯认为这是他多年来一直在进行的文化战争的延伸。

sentences.en: Because Mike Davis saw this as an extension of the culture wars that he's been fighting for years.

sentences.en: Exactly.

sentences.en: The Democrats brought the perfect storm here.

sentences.en: It was the Me Too cultural clash with a judicial fight, and it was just a fight that I was not going to back down from.
sentences.zh: 这是“我也是”运动的文化冲突与司法斗争的交织，而这是一场我绝不会退缩的斗争。

sentences.en: So for Davis, this is a historic moment, and he's ready to pull out all the stops.

sentences.en: We'll be right back.

sentences.en: So, Robin, Kate, what does the Mike Davis playbook look like when he actually tries to protect Brett Kavanaugh?
sentences.zh: 那么，罗宾，凯特，当迈克·戴维斯真正试图保护布雷特·卡瓦诺时，他的行动手册是什么样的？

sentences.en: So there are sort of four key tenets to it.
sentences.zh: 这里面大概有四个核心要点。

sentences.en: The first one is after a quick assessment of the facts and a feeling of confidence that the issue can be overcome,
sentences.zh: 第一点是，在对事实进行快速评估并确信问题能够克服之后，

sentences.en: that's when you message to your entire support network that you are going to stay the course.
sentences.zh: 这时你要向你的整个支持网络传达一个信息：你将坚持到底。

sentences.en: On September 20th, Kavanaugh was on life support and Republicans were running for the hills.
sentences.zh: 在9月20日，卡瓦诺已经奄奄一息，共和党人则吓得四处逃窜。

sentences.en: And what I wanted to do was send out a message that there was someone inside that Senate Judiciary Committee fighting.
sentences.zh: 而我想做的是发出一个信号：参议院司法委员会内部还有人在战斗。

sentences.en: It was a bat signal.
sentences.zh: 这是一个蝙蝠侠信号。

sentences.en: So that's where you see something like a September 20th tweet from Mike Davis saying, unfazed and determined, we will confirm Judge Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么你会看到迈克·戴维斯在9月20日发推文说，我们镇定自若、坚定不移，必将确认卡瓦诺法官。

sentences.en: That's days after Christine Blasey Ford has come public and Kavanaugh is very much in doubt in terms of whether his candidacy can move forward.
sentences.zh: 那是克里斯蒂娜·布莱西·福德公开露面几天后，卡瓦诺的提名能否推进充满巨大变数。
zh_words: 克里斯蒂娜·布莱西·福德

sentences.en: So almost immediately, Davis is rushing to his rhetorical defense.
sentences.zh: 因此，几乎立刻，戴维斯就冲出来进行言论辩护。

sentences.en: It was to say that these allegations are not adding up.
sentences.zh: 这就是要说明这些指控根本站不住脚。

sentences.en: The lawyers are playing games and we do not have a presumption of guilt in this country.
sentences.zh: 律师们在玩弄把戏，在这个国家，我们没有有罪推定。

sentences.en: Number two is to turn the accused into the victim.
sentences.zh: 第二点是将被告变成受害者。

sentences.en: In the case of Kavanaugh, that was to make the argument that Kavanaugh has already been evaluated by the FBI.
sentences.zh: 就卡瓦诺而言，就是提出这样的论点：卡瓦诺已经接受过联邦调查局的审查。

sentences.en: He was a judge on the D.C.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任哥伦比亚特区

sentences.en: circuit for 12 years, the second highest court in the land.
sentences.zh: 巡回法院法官12年，这是全国第二高法院。

sentences.en: He had six, now seven, FBI full-field, single-scope background investigations.
sentences.zh: 他经历过六次，现在是七次，联邦调查局全面的、单一范围的背景调查。

sentences.en: They talked to 160 people who knew him beSt.
sentences.zh: 他们与160个最了解他的人交谈过。

sentences.en: This guy has already passed the teSt.
sentences.zh: 这家伙已经通过了考验。

sentences.en: Look what you're putting him through again.
sentences.zh: 看看你们又在让他经历什么。

sentences.en: You're potentially ruining his family and his career.
sentences.zh: 你们可能正在毁掉他的家庭和他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: There was not a whiff of impropriety related to alcoholism or sexual abuse.
sentences.zh: 没有任何迹象表明他与酗酒或性虐待有任何不正当行为。

sentences.en: You're dragging his name through the mud.
sentences.zh: 你们在把他的名声搞得身败名裂。

sentences.en: You haven't given this guy a fair trial and you're already convicting him.
sentences.zh: 你们没有给这个人公正的审判，就已经在给他定罪了。

sentences.en: In the Me Too era, we're just supposed to say, you know what, let's just throw due process out the door.
sentences.zh: 在“我也是”运动时代，我们本该说，你知道吗，让我们把正当程序抛到脑后吧。

sentences.en: Let's just throw the presumption of innocence out the door.
sentences.zh: 让我们把无罪推定抛到脑后吧。

sentences.en: Let's, you know, let's do this un-American presumption of guilt because we're the Me Too era.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，让我们搞这种不符合美国传统的有罪推定吧，因为我们正处于“我也是”运动时代。

sentences.en: That is garbage.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是垃圾。

sentences.en: And we were not going to let that happen to a good man like Justice Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不会让这种事发生在像卡瓦诺大法官这样的好人身上。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to flesh out and understand better the accusations themselves.
sentences.zh: 而不是去厘清和更好地理解指控本身。

sentences.en: The third tenet deals with casting doubt upon the facts and also tarnishing or perhaps politicizing the accuser.
sentences.zh: 第三个要点是质疑事实，并玷污或可能将原告政治化。

sentences.en: Listen, I don't believe Dr. Ford's allegations.
sentences.zh: 听着，我不相信福德医生的指控。

sentences.en: I don't think she's telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 我不认为她在说实话。

sentences.en: Tell us why.
sentences.zh: 告诉我们为什么。

sentences.en: There's just so many holes in her story and, you know, little fibs here and there.
sentences.zh: 她的故事里有太多的漏洞，你知道的，还有一些大大小小的谎言。

sentences.en: And when people make little fibs on things that are smaller, well, they also fib about bigger things.
sentences.zh: 当人们在小事情上撒小谎时，嗯，他们在大事上也会撒谎。

sentences.en: I just don't know.
sentences.zh: 我只是不知道。

sentences.en: You saw that with Dr. Ford with some of the issues about fear of flying.
sentences.zh: 你在福德医生关于害怕坐飞机的一些问题上看到了这一点。

sentences.en: She said that she had a Kavanaugh-induced fear of flying so she couldn't come out to the hearing on a certain date.
sentences.zh: 她说她有一种卡瓦诺引发的恐飞症，所以她不能在某个特定日期出席听证会。

sentences.en: The CV that she submitted to the committee shows as one of her interests international surf travel to places like Hawaii and Australia and all over the world.
sentences.zh: 她提交给委员会的简历显示，她的兴趣之一是前往夏威夷、澳大利亚和世界各地进行国际冲浪旅行。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking, hmm, if she has this Kavanaugh-induced fear of flying, how did she get to Australia?
sentences.zh: 我在想，嗯，如果她有这种卡瓦诺引发的恐飞症，她是怎么去澳大利亚的？

sentences.en: Did she surf there?
sentences.zh: 她在那里冲浪了吗？

sentences.en: Raising doubts about all those sorts of things as well as pointing to a lack of evidence or evidence that might suggest that the story is inaccurate.
sentences.zh: 对所有这些事情提出质疑，同时指出缺乏证据或可能表明故事不准确的证据。

sentences.en: Even if the issue that's being disputed is way off to the side.
sentences.zh: 即使被争议的问题完全是题外话。

sentences.en: She has no memory of key details of the night in question.
sentences.zh: 她对那个关键夜晚的关键细节毫无记忆。

sentences.en: She doesn't remember who invited her to the party or how she heard about it.
sentences.zh: 她不记得是谁邀请她去派对的，也不记得她是怎么知道这个派对的。

sentences.en: She doesn't remember how she got to the party.
sentences.zh: 她不记得她是怎么去派对的。

sentences.en: She doesn't remember what house...
sentences.zh: 她不记得是哪栋房子……

sentences.en: And that is simply a way to put a seed of doubt in an already skeptical person's mind about this account.
sentences.zh: 这简直是在一个本已怀疑的人心中埋下怀疑的种子，让他们对这种说法产生动摇。

sentences.en: And number four is to frame this all in the context of a partisan battle.
sentences.zh: 第四点是将这一切置于党派斗争的背景下来构建。

sentences.en: It's the whole way this process was handled.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个过程的处理方式。

sentences.en: It was the gamesmanship.
sentences.zh: 这就是政治手腕。

sentences.en: It was Dianne Feinstein sitting on this letter for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 这就是黛安·范斯坦把这封信压了六周。

sentences.en: It was this partisan hack lawyer who is, you know, representing Christine Blasey Ford using her.
sentences.zh: 这就是这个代表克里斯蒂娜·布莱西·福德的党派御用律师在利用她。
zh_words: 克里斯蒂娜·布莱西·福德

sentences.en: That this is a conspiracy, that it's a witch hunt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个阴谋，这是一场政治迫害。

sentences.en: And some of the language around this speaks to that, this real hyperbolic, huge sweeping statements like a calculated, orchestrated political hit,
sentences.zh: 围绕这一点的一些言论说明了这一点，这些极其夸张、一概而论的大话，比如精心策划的政治暗杀，

sentences.en: which were the words of Brett Kavanaugh.
sentences.zh: 这是布雷特·卡瓦诺的原话。

sentences.en: I think this whole process was disgusting.
sentences.zh: 我认为整个过程令人作呕。

sentences.en: And it was transparently political to me.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这是赤裸裸的政治操弄。

sentences.en: What that does is it removes us from the facts on the ground in terms of whether these allegations have any legitimacy and should be explored in any real way.
sentences.zh: 这样做让我们脱离了实地事实，无法判断这些指控是否具有合法性，是否应该以任何真正的方式进行调查。

sentences.en: And it takes it to the level of this is all just politics.
sentences.zh: 它把问题上升到了这纯粹是政治斗争的高度。

sentences.en: And Mike Davis has an analogy for what they're doing here.
sentences.zh: 迈克·戴维斯对他们在这里做的事情有一个比喻。

sentences.en: You know, what I did with with Kavanaugh's confirmation, I called it the dead chicken strategy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我对卡瓦诺的确认听证会所做的事，我称之为死鸡策略。

sentences.en: What on earth does that mean?
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: What is the dead chicken strategy?
sentences.zh: 什么是死鸡策略？

sentences.en: So remember that Davis, for a brief period, was a clerk for the newly installed Justice Gorsuch.
sentences.zh: 请记住，戴维斯曾在新上任的戈萨奇大法官手下做过短暂的书记员。

sentences.en: And during that clerkship, the clerks would get together for lunch with individual justices.
sentences.zh: 在那段书记员任期内，书记员们会和个别大法官一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: Davis had a lunch with Justice Clarence Thomas.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯和克拉伦斯·托马斯大法官共进过午餐。

sentences.en: And during that lunch, Thomas told this story about growing up on a farm in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 在那次午餐中，托马斯讲了一个他在佐治亚州农场长大的故事。

sentences.en: He said when dogs killed chickens, they would take those chickens and wrap it around those dogs' necks.
sentences.zh: 他说，当狗咬死鸡时，人们会把那些鸡挂在那些狗的脖子上。

sentences.en: And as those chickens rot it around those dogs' necks, those dogs lost the taste for chicken.
sentences.zh: 当那些鸡在这些狗的脖子上腐烂时，这些狗就失去了对鸡肉的兴趣。

sentences.en: And I think that's what Republicans need to start doing with the left.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是共和党人需要对左翼做的事情。

sentences.en: Davis sees this as an analogy to what needs to be done to the liberals to punish them for their tactics.
sentences.zh: 戴维斯认为这是一个比喻，说明需要对自由派采取什么行动来惩罚他们的战术。

sentences.en: So who exactly are the characters in this colorful metaphor?
sentences.zh: 那么，这个色彩丰富的隐喻中的角色到底是谁呢？

sentences.en: So in this case, the chicken is essentially the smears and lies that Davis believes that liberals have told about their political opponents.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个案例中，鸡基本上就是戴维斯认为自由派针对其政治对手散布的污蔑和谎言。

sentences.en: Whether it was Judge Kavanaugh, whether it is President Trump, or any others who are part of the conservative objectives that Davis espouses.
sentences.zh: 无论是卡瓦诺法官，特朗普总统，还是任何其他支持戴维斯所倡导的保守派目标的人。

sentences.en: And they need to be punished and given a taste of their own medicine and have those smears pushed back in their face in order for them to lose the taste for that kind of political war-making.
sentences.zh: 他们必须受到惩罚，让他们尝尝自己的苦果，把那些污蔑反弹到他们脸上，这样他们就会失去发动那种政治战争的兴趣。

sentences.en: So because the Kavanaugh strategy worked so effectively, we wanted to ask Mike Davis the question, how is that playbook working for the Trump administration now,
sentences.zh: 因此，由于卡瓦诺的策略非常有效，我们想问迈克·戴维斯一个问题，这套策略现在对特朗普政府是如何起作用的，

sentences.en: as the conservatives are facing a very real threat to President Trump in the form of impeachment?
sentences.zh: 因为保守派正面临着以弹劾形式出现的对特朗普总统的现实威胁？

sentences.en: And what does he say?
sentences.zh: 他是怎么说的？

sentences.en: He says we're seeing it unfold before our very eyes as it comes to handling the impeachment inquiry and defending an embattled President Trump.
sentences.zh: 他说，在处理弹劾调查和捍卫陷入困境的特朗普总统时，我们正亲眼目睹这一切的展开。

sentences.en: So you start with forceful denials and assertions that there was no wrongdoing on the part of the president.
sentences.zh: 所以你首先要强力否认，并断言总统没有任何不当行为。

sentences.en: Impeachment should be a last resort.
sentences.zh: 弹劾应该是最后的手段。

sentences.en: It is for high crimes and misdemeanors.
sentences.zh: 它是针对严重罪行和轻罪的。

sentences.en: And nothing that has been alleged against President Trump even comes close to those, even if these allegations are true, which they're not.
sentences.zh: 指控特朗普总统的任何事情甚至都沾不上边，即使这些指控是真的，然而它们并不是真的。

sentences.en: It doesn't even come close.
sentences.zh: 连边都沾不上。

sentences.en: You then go to a discrediting of political opponents, of whistleblowers, or even the people that leaked to the original whistleblower.
sentences.zh: 然后你要去抹黑政治对手、吹哨人，甚至向最初吹哨人泄密的人。

sentences.en: Were they politically motivated?
sentences.zh: 他们有政治动机吗？

sentences.en: Did they do the right thing?
sentences.zh: 他们做对了吗？

sentences.en: Then there's an attack on the facts and whether or not they're legitimate.
sentences.zh: 接着是对事实以及它们是否合法发起攻击。

sentences.en: With their outrageous lies and smears and impeachment mobs and Me Too mobs, we need to fight back as conservatives, as Republicans, because the left has a glass jaw.
sentences.zh: 面对他们无耻的谎言、污蔑、弹劾暴徒和“我也是”暴徒，作为保守派、作为共和党人，我们需要反击，因为左翼有着脆弱的下巴。

sentences.en: And if you fight back, you'll break their glass jaw.
sentences.zh: 如果你进行反击，你就会击碎他们脆弱的下巴。

sentences.en: And then finally, there's an invocation of this sort of the witch hunt, the persecution of the president,
sentences.zh: 最后，是援引这种政治迫害、对总统的迫害，

sentences.en: how un-American this is and how inherently and disgustingly political it has become.
sentences.zh: 这有多么不符合美国传统，以及它变得多么本质上、令人作呕地政治化。

sentences.en: This is the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这是美利坚合众国的总统。

sentences.en: He was elected by the American people, whether the left likes it or not.
sentences.zh: 无论左翼喜欢与否，他都是由美国人民选举产生的。

sentences.en: And just to stay with your chicken metaphor and clarify it, what's the dead chicken and around whose neck in this case?
sentences.zh: 为了顺着你的死鸡比喻并澄清一下，在这种情况下，死鸡是什么，挂在谁的脖子上？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I think right now you're looking at Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我觉得你现在看到的是乔·拜登。

sentences.en: The Democrats are going to hurt the one Democrat who has a shot at beating Trump by bringing in this whole Ukraine corruption mess.
sentences.zh: 民主党人通过引入整个乌克兰腐败烂摊子，将伤害唯一有机会击败特朗普的民主党人。

sentences.en: Because Joe Biden has his own problems with this Ukraine corruption mess.
sentences.zh: 因为乔·拜登在这个乌克兰腐败烂摊子上也有他自己的问题。

sentences.en: So be careful, Democrats, what you – this impeachment can of worMs.
sentences.zh: 所以，民主党人，小心你们的言行——这场弹劾是个潘多拉魔盒。

sentences.en: So if the dead chicken strategy succeeds in the case of impeachment the way it sounds like he thinks it succeeded in the case of Kavanaugh,
sentences.zh: 因此，如果死鸡策略在弹劾案中取得成功，正如他认为在卡瓦诺案中取得成功那样，

sentences.en: then Democrats will stop pursuing impeachment because they will see the flaws in their arguments about why he should be impeached?
sentences.zh: 那么民主党人就会停止推进弹劾，因为他们会看到他们关于为什么要弹劾他的论点的漏洞？

sentences.en: I think it's even deeper than that.
sentences.zh: 我认为比那还要深远。

sentences.en: I think it's that, but it's also perhaps his belief that Democrats need to check their own motives and realize that this person has been elected and he's here at least until 2021.
sentences.zh: 我认为不仅如此，或许还包括他的信念，即民主党人需要反省自己的动机，认识到这个人是选出来的，他至少会干到2021年。

sentences.en: And that they need to just be governed by this president and focus on legislation and other issues,
sentences.zh: 他们需要接受这位总统的统治，专注于立法和其他问题，

sentences.en: but drop the political animus and the tools he believes they are using to achieve political ends, which in his mind are smears and lies, among other things.
sentences.zh: 但要抛弃政治敌意以及他认为他们用来达到政治目的的工具，在他看来，这些工具除其他外就是污蔑和谎言。

sentences.en: I wonder, though, if Mike Davis is right,
sentences.zh: 不过我很好奇，如果迈克·戴维斯是对的，

sentences.en: that the same strategy that Republicans used successfully to confirm Brett Kavanaugh can work to fend off impeachment for President Trump because the situations are quite different.
sentences.zh: 共和党人用来成功确认布雷特·卡瓦诺的同一策略可以用来为特朗普总统抵御弹劾，因为这两种情况截然不同。

sentences.en: One was a debate over what happened decades ago when people were in high school and memories were hazier and witnesses not available to corroborate something.
sentences.zh: 一个是关于几十年前人们还在高中时发生的事情的辩论，当时的记忆更模糊，也没有证人来佐证某些事。

sentences.en: Here, in the case of the Ukraine phone call, there is a transcript.
sentences.zh: 而在乌克兰电话门的这个案例中，有文字记录。

sentences.en: There are people who listened in on the call and there were whistleblowers to something that happened just about a month ago.
sentences.zh: 有旁听通话的人，还有针对大约一个月前发生的事情的吹哨人。

sentences.en: So are these fundamentally different?
sentences.zh: 所以这些有根本的不同吗？

sentences.en: I think actually the template can still be applied to a very different set of circumstances because the ultimate goal is to win.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为这个模板仍然可以应用于一组非常不同的情况，因为最终的目标是获胜。

sentences.en: And so what you do is you remove this from the facts and you take it out of the substance.
sentences.zh: 所以你要做的就是把这从事实中剥离出来，脱离其实质内容。

sentences.en: And it's all about this sweeping general statement that this is a political hit job and that's all you need to know and keep focused on the fact that we have to defend this guy against a broad-based effort to take him down.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一个一概而论的宏大陈述，即这是一场政治暗杀，这就是你需要知道的全部，并专注于这样一个事实：我们必须保护这个人，免受旨在搞垮他的广泛努力的侵害。

sentences.en: And don't lose sight of the thing that undergirds this whole effort, which is the conservative culture war.
sentences.zh: 不要忽视支撑这一切的核心，那就是保守派文化战争。

sentences.en: Mike Davis, President Trump, and others have a vision for how the courts should look, how the country should look,
sentences.zh: 迈克·戴维斯、特朗普总统和其他人对法院应该是什么样子、国家应该是什么样子有着宏伟愿景，

sentences.en: and they are trying their level best to get to that through whatever means necessary.
sentences.zh: 他们正竭尽全力通过一切必要手段来实现这一目标。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so efforts to stop it may take many forms, but they are in this telling and through this playbook all a part of the same effort to just stymie this.
sentences.zh: 因此，阻止它的努力可能采取多种形式，但在这种说法和这套行动手册中，它们都是为了阻挠这一进程的同一努力的一部分。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: The interesting hitch in this kind of well-developed strategy is that if the person in question looks to be on the ropes, if it looks as if this battle is not going to be won,
sentences.zh: 这种精心制定的策略中有一个有趣的转折：如果当事人看起来处于劣势，如果这场战斗看起来赢不了，

sentences.en: there is a kind of an exit strategy, an escape hatch, if you will.
sentences.zh: 就会有一种退出策略，如果你愿意的话，可以叫逃生舱口。

sentences.en: And in the case of President Trump, that might mean that if it feels as if there is not enough political will to survive this battle,
sentences.zh: 在特朗普总统的情况下，这意味着如果感觉没有足够的政治意愿来挺过这场战斗，

sentences.en: there is a scenario in which you could imagine a guy like Mike Davis walking away.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象一种场景，像迈克·戴维斯这样的人会选择走开。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because ultimately the most important thing is this larger culture war, not the individuals you're fighting for.
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，最重要的是这场更大的文化战争，而不是你所支持的个人。

sentences.en: So if it looks like the country does support not just impeachment, but removing the president from office or not re-electing him,
sentences.zh: 所以如果看起来这个国家不仅支持弹劾，还支持解除总统职务或不让他连任，

sentences.en: you could foresee a day where the great warriors in this battle, the Mike Davises, might just wash their hands of it.
sentences.zh: 你可以预见到这样一天：这场战斗中的伟大战士，比如迈克·戴维斯，可能会直接洗手不干。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because the important thing is to have the big picture in mind.
sentences.zh: 因为重要的是要放眼大局。

sentences.en: And the big picture is they want to transform this country and they're going to do whatever it takes to do that.
sentences.zh: 大局是他们想要改造这个国家，为了做到这一点，他们会不择手段。

sentences.en: And if there are casualties along the way, including the president, so be it.
sentences.zh: 如果一路上出现牺牲品，包括总统在内，那就这样吧。

sentences.en: Thank you both very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的内容。

sentences.en: We witnessed the beginning of this offensive at around about four o'clock local time this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 我们目睹了这场攻势的开始，大约是在今天下午当地时间四点左右。

sentences.en: A series of loud explosions.
sentences.zh: 伴随着一连串巨大的爆炸声。

sentences.en: You can probably hear more of them now.
sentences.zh: 你现在可能还能听到更多。

sentences.en: And it's been pretty constant.
sentences.zh: 而且这种声音一直相当持续。

sentences.en: On Wednesday, Turkey began a military assault on northeast Syria, launching airstrikes and firing artillery against American-backed Kurdish forces there.
sentences.zh: 周三，土耳其对叙利亚东北部发动了军事进攻，对当地受到美国支持的库尔德武装发动了空袭和炮击。

sentences.en: Volleys of artillery from our location in southern Turkey being fired across the border onto Kurdish positions in northern Syria.
sentences.zh: 在我们位于土耳其南部的位置，可以看到炮弹齐射跨越边界，射向叙利亚北部的库尔德人阵地。

sentences.en: The attack only began after President Trump approved it during a telephone call over the weekend with Turkey's president.
sentences.zh: 这次袭击是在特朗普总统在周末与土耳其总统通电话时批准后才开始的。

sentences.en: But on Wednesday, Trump seemed to regret that decision, saying in a statement that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但在周三，特朗普似乎对那个决定感到后悔，他在一份声明中表示，美国

sentences.en: quote, does not endorse this attack and thinks it's a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 引述原话，不支持这次袭击，并认为这是一个坏主意。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 还有。

sentences.en: Batteries, extra lighting, flashlights.
sentences.zh: 电池、额外照明、手电筒。

sentences.en: I have extra flashlights at home.
sentences.zh: 我家里有多余的手电筒。

sentences.en: I bought some ceiling lights.
sentences.zh: 我买了一些顶灯。

sentences.en: And then I'm going to try to preserve as much of my food as I can with the ice.
sentences.zh: 然后我打算用冰块尽可能地保存我的食物。

sentences.en: In an unusual move,
sentences.zh: 在一项不同寻常的举动中，

sentences.en: the largest utility in California is deliberately cutting off power to at least two million residents to avoid the possibility of wildfires over the next few days.
sentences.zh: 加州最大的公用事业公司正在故意切断至少两百万居民的电源，以避免在未来几天内发生野火的可能性。

sentences.en: Forecasts for hot, dry air and winds of up to 70 miles per hour have created a high risk of fires started by downed power lines,
sentences.zh: 天气预报显示将有炎热干燥的空气和高达每小时70英里的风速，这造成了由倒塌的电线引发火灾的高风险，

sentences.en: the cause of several previous wildfires across California.
sentences.zh: 这也是加州过去几场野火的原因。

sentences.en: We very much understand the inconvenience and difficulties such a power outage would cause.
sentences.zh: 我们非常理解这种停电会带来的不便和困难。

sentences.en: And we do not take or make this decision lightly.
sentences.zh: 而且我们做出这个决定并非轻率之举。

sentences.en: The power outages have disrupted life across the state, with schools canceling classes, stores closing their doors and drivers navigating streets without working traffic lights,
sentences.zh: 大面积停电打乱了全州的生活，学校取消课程，商店关门大吉，司机们在没有红绿灯的街道上艰难行驶，

sentences.en: angering residents and prompting the utility, PG&E, to defend its decision.
sentences.zh: 这激怒了居民，并促使该公用事业公司太平洋天然气与电力公司为自己的决定进行辩护。

sentences.en: We implement the public safety power shutoff as a last resort.
sentences.zh: 我们实施公共安全断电是作为最后的手段。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日简报》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一个受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了（迎来了）一群自称为改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又惊心动魄的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持其影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你获取播客的任何平台上收听。
